hook.text: Why can a metal part fail even when no single load is large enough to break it?

define.text: Fatigue is damage from repeated loading. It can occur when nominal stress stays below yield strength.

photo.text: This is a real fractured bolt from published research.

root.text: The paper notes that fatigue commonly occurs at thread roots.

unmapped.text: The exact origin is not mapped here.

surfaces.text: Fatigue surfaces may show smoother growth regions and rougher final fracture; appearances vary.

initiation.text: A scratch concentrates stress locally, and a small crack begins.

growth.text: As cycle count N increases, crack length a grows, leaving less intact material.

hidden.text: The gradual growth may be hard to see. The sudden break is only the final stage.

fracture.text: Once the crack reaches a critical condition, the remaining section fractures rapidly.

sn_intro.text: An S N curve connects stress amplitude to fatigue life.

amplitude.text: S is half the difference between maximum and minimum stress.

axis_s.text: The vertical axis is stress amplitude in megapascals.

axis_n.text: The horizontal axis shows cycles to failure on a logarithmic scale.

sn_read.text: Choose a stress, move across to the curve, then down to read life.

lower.text: For the same material and conditions, lower amplitude usually means longer life.

steel.text: Some steels show a fatigue limit under specific test conditions.

aluminum.text: Aluminum alloys generally do not. These limits are not universal safety guarantees.

toughness.text: Fracture toughness measures resistance to fracture with a crack.

ki.text: K eye describes crack tip loading: the Mode one stress intensity factor.

symbols.text: Y describes geometry; sigma is tensile stress; a measures edge to tip.

compare.text: Raising stress or lengthening the crack increases K eye.

kic.text: K eye see is material plane strain fracture toughness, not yield strength.

critical.text: Under linear elastic, valid plane strain conditions, peak K eye reaching K eye see can trigger rapid fracture.

subcritical.text: Fatigue cracks can grow below this limit.

recap1.text: Repeated loading can cause fatigue damage.

recap2.text: S N curves relate stress amplitude to fatigue life.

recap3.text: Fracture toughness helps assess when an existing crack becomes critical.

engineering.text: Reduce stress concentrations, improve surface condition, and inspect for cracks to reduce fatigue risk.

credits.text: These sources support the lesson. Full links, photo credits, and reproducible code accompany this video.
